title: AEE 2026 Fellowship: Research, Learning and Preservation of Ebira Knowledge, Culture and Heritage
summary: The AEE 2026 Fellowship is an opportunity for students, researchers, graduates, writers, creatives, early-career professionals and other individuals interested in Ebira history, culture, language, heritage and contemporary issues to engage in structured learning, research and knowledge production. Held under the theme “Research, Learning and the Preservation of Ebira Knowledge, Culture and Heritage,” the fellowship is designed to encourage deeper exploration and documentation of Ebira knowledge and cultural heritage while giving participants an opportunity to develop research ideas and produce written work based on their interests. The application process requires prospective fellows to provide information about their personal background, education, professional experience, research interests, motivation and availability to participate in the fellowship. Applicants are also expected to indicate their willingness to undertake an individual research project, produce a scholarly article and actively participate in fellowship activities. About the AEE 2026 Fellowship The AEE 2026 Fellowship focuses on the relationship between research, learning, cultural knowledge and heritage preservation . Through the programme, participants are expected to explore subjects connected to Ebira society and contribute to the documentation and preservation of knowledge that may be important to present and future generations. The fellowship provides a platform for participants with different educational and professional backgrounds to identify areas of interest and develop them into research topics or ideas. The application form specifically invites applicants to consider subjects including Ebira history, culture and tradition, language, literature, heritage preservation, history, political and development studies, as well as contemporary issues. Rather than limiting applicants to a single academic discipline, the fellowship appears to encourage multidisciplinary engagement with Ebira knowledge and heritage. This allows participants to approach the study of Ebira society from different perspectives, depending on their academic background, professional experience, creative interests or research goals. Fellowship Theme The official theme of the programme is: “Research, Learning and the Preservation of Ebira Knowledge, Culture and Heritage.” The theme highlights several interconnected areas: Research: Encouraging participants to investigate topics relating to Ebira history, culture, language, heritage and contemporary society. Learning: Providing an environment in which participants can develop their understanding of research and knowledge production. Knowledge preservation: Supporting the documentation and continuation of Ebira knowledge for current and future generations. Cultural heritage: Promoting research and engagement with traditions, historical experiences, language, literature and other aspects of Ebira heritage. Knowledge production: Encouraging participants to transform their interests and research ideas into structured written work. Areas of Interest Covered by the Fellowship Applicants are asked to identify the areas in which they have an interest. These include: 1. Ebira History Participants can explore historical aspects of Ebiraland, including important events, communities, historical figures, social developments and other subjects that contribute to an understanding of Ebira history. Research in this area may involve examining historical records, oral histories, community narratives or other sources of knowledge. 2. Ebira Culture and Tradition The fellowship also provides an avenue for exploring Ebira culture and traditional practices. Applicants interested in this area may consider different aspects of cultural identity, customs, traditions, social practices and community knowledge. 3. Ebira Language Language is an important component of cultural preservation. Applicants may therefore develop research ideas relating to the Ebira language, including its preservation, use, development, documentation, literature or role in cultural identity. 4. Heritage and Cultural Preservation Applicants can investigate ways in which Ebira cultural heritage and knowledge can be documented, protected and passed to future generations. This area may be particularly relevant to individuals interested in cultural documentation, heritage studies, community-based research and preservation initiatives. 5. Literature The fellowship welcomes interests relating to literature. Applicants may explore literary works, storytelling, oral traditions, written literature or the relationship between literature and Ebira identity and culture. 6. History Beyond specifically defined Ebira historical subjects, applicants can also indicate a broader interest in history and develop a research idea relevant to the fellowship theme. 7. Political Studies Political issues and political developments are also included among the listed areas of interest. Applicants can therefore propose research examining political questions connected to Ebira society or relevant contemporary contexts. 8. Development Studies Development-related research is another area identified in the application form. Potential research interests may examine social, economic, institutional or community development issues relevant to Ebiraland. 9. Contemporary Issues The fellowship also recognizes the importance of studying current issues affecting Ebira communities and society. Applicants can therefore develop research proposals addressing contemporary challenges, developments or emerging questions. 10. Other Areas Applicants are also given an “Other” option, allowing them to identify an area of interest that is not explicitly included in the listed categories. Who Can Apply for the AEE 2026 Fellowship? The application form accommodates people at different stages of their academic, research, professional and creative journeys. Applicants are asked to select their current status from the following categories: Undergraduate students Postgraduate students Researchers Graduates Early-career professionals Writers and creatives Other applicants whose status does not fit the listed categories The form also asks applicants to provide their institution or organisation, course of study or area of specialization, and highest educational qualification. Educational Qualifications Applicants are asked to indicate their highest educational qualification from the following options: Secondary School OND/NCE HND/Bachelor s Degree Master s Degree PhD Other qualifications This indicates that the application form is structured to accommodate applicants with different levels of educational attainment rather than being restricted solely to postgraduate researchers or degree holders. Ebira Indigene Requirement One of the specific questions in the application form asks: “Are you an indigene of Ebiraland?” Applicants are required to select either Yes or No . Those who answer yes are subsequently asked to specify which part or Local Government Area of Ebiraland they are from . Because the application form specifically asks about Ebira indigene status and the applicant s part/LGA of Ebiraland, prospective applicants should pay close attention to this section and provide accurate information about their background. Research Experience and Knowledge Production The AEE 2026 Fellowship places significant emphasis on research, writing and knowledge production. Applicants are asked whether they have previous experience in: Research Writing Cultural activities Knowledge production They can respond either Yes or No . Previous experience is therefore directly addressed in the application, although the form does not state that applicants must already have extensive research experience. This makes it important for applicants to accurately describe any relevant experience they have, whether it comes from academic research, independent writing, cultural activities, community engagement, documentation, creative work or other forms of knowledge production. Proposed Research Topic A major component of the application involves identifying what the applicant would like to research. Applicants are asked: “What aspect of Ebira history, culture, language, heritage or contemporary issues would you like to research?” They are then required to briefly describe their proposed research topic or idea . This section gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate the subject they would like to investigate during the fellowship. A strong response should clearly communicate: The subject the applicant wants to investigate. The specific issue or question they are interested in. Why the subject is relevant to Ebira knowledge, culture, history, language, heritage or contemporary society. What they hope to understand, document or contribute through the research. Applicants should ensure that their proposed topic is realistic and sufficiently focused to be developed into an individual research project during the fellowship. Why Participate in the AEE 2026 Fellowship? The application form indicates that participants will be expected to engage in a structured eight-week fellowship involving research, learning and other activities. Potential areas of engagement include: Research Development Participants will have an opportunity to develop an individual research project around an aspect of Ebira history, culture, language, heritage or contemporary issues. Scholarly Writing Participants are expected to write and submit a scholarly article based on their research. This can provide practical experience in transforming a research idea into a structured written output. Knowledge Preservation By researching and documenting aspects of Ebira knowledge, culture and heritage, participants can contribute to broader efforts to preserve cultural knowledge. Discussions and Presentations The fellowship requires participants to take part in discussions, presentations, assignments and other programme activities. This creates opportunities for participants to engage with ideas and communicate their research interests. Research and Cultural Engagement Participants can use the fellowship as an opportunity to deepen their engagement with subjects relating to Ebira identity, history, language, traditions and contemporary development. Eight-Week Fellowship Commitment Applicants must confirm whether they are available to participate in the eight-week fellowship every Saturday and Sunday . This is an important consideration before applying. Prospective applicants should ensure that they can consistently participate throughout the programme period. The application form asks applicants to confirm their availability by selecting either: Yes No Applicants should provide an accurate response because successful participation is expected to require a sustained commitment over the eight-week period. Individual Research Project Participants are asked whether they are willing to complete an individual research project during the fellowship. The research project is a central component of the programme and connects directly to the fellowship s broader emphasis on research, learning and preservation of Ebira knowledge. Applicants should therefore consider their potential research interests before completing the application and think about a topic that they could realistically investigate during the programme. Scholarly Article Requirement The fellowship also asks applicants whether they are willing to write and submit a scholarly article based on their research . This means participants should be prepared not only to identify a research topic but also to develop their findings into a written scholarly output. For prospective applicants, this requirement makes writing ability, willingness to conduct research and commitment to completing written work particularly relevant to the fellowship. Participation in Fellowship Activities Applicants are required to indicate whether they are willing to participate in: Discussions Presentations Assignments Other fellowship activities Participation is therefore not limited to independent research. Successful fellows are expected to engage with the wider programme and its activities. Previous Fellowship and Training Experience The application form also asks whether applicants have previously participated in: Fellowships Research programmes Training programmes Similar programmes Applicants can answer either Yes or No . Those with previous experience should provide truthful information when completing the application. Applicants without previous fellowship or research programme experience can also indicate that they have not participated in such programmes. What Applicants Hope to Gain The application includes a question asking: “What do you hope to gain from the AEE 2026 Fellowship?” This gives applicants an opportunity to explain their expectations and learning objectives. Applicants may wish to discuss goals connected to research development, scholarly writing, cultural knowledge, heritage preservation, academic development, networking, knowledge production or gaining practical experience in investigating and documenting Ebira-related subjects. The strongest response should connect the applicant s personal or professional objectives with the focus of the fellowship. Personal and Contact Information Required Applicants must provide several pieces of personal information as part of the application process. These include: Full name Date of birth Gender Phone number Email address State of residence Local Government Area Ebira indigene status Part/LGA of Ebiraland, where applicable Applicants should carefully check these details before submitting the form to ensure that all information is accurate. Academic and Professional Information Required The education and professional section asks applicants to provide: Current status Institution or organisation Course of study or area of specialization Highest educational qualification The current-status options include undergraduate student, postgraduate student, researcher, graduate, early-career professional, writer/creative and other. Application Declaration Before submitting the application, candidates are required to confirm that the information they have provided is true and correct to the best of their knowledge . The declaration also acknowledges that participation in the AEE 2026 Fellowship requires commitment to: The fellowship programme The research project Other fellowship activities Applicants should therefore review their responses carefully before submitting the form. How to Apply for the AEE 2026 Fellowship Interested applicants should complete the AEE 2026 Fellowship Application Form and provide the requested personal, educational, professional and research information. The application process involves the following general steps: Complete the personal information section. Provide your educational and professional background. Identify your areas of interest. Explain your motivation for joining the fellowship. Indicate whether you have previous research, writing, cultural or knowledge-production experience. Identify the aspect of Ebira history, culture, language, heritage or contemporary issues you would like to research. Describe your proposed research topic or idea. Confirm your availability for the eight-week weekend fellowship. Confirm your willingness to undertake an individual research project. Confirm your willingness to write and submit a scholarly article. Confirm your willingness to participate in discussions, presentations, assignments and other activities. Provide information about previous fellowship, research or training experience. Explain what you hope to gain from the programme. Complete the declaration and submit the application. Applicants should ensure that their responses are accurate, complete and relevant to the fellowship s theme. APPLY HERE AEE 2026 Fellowship Deadline Deadline: Not specified in the provided application form. The supplied AEE 2026 Fellowship application information does not state a closing date. Applicants should therefore check the official application page or announcement for any deadline or subsequent update before submitting their application. Important Information for Applicants Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted , according to the application form. Applicants should therefore: Provide accurate contact information. Ensure all required questions are answered. Clearly explain their motivation for applying. Present a focused research topic or idea. Demonstrate genuine interest in Ebira knowledge, culture, heritage or related contemporary issues. Consider whether they can commit to the eight-week Saturday and Sunday schedule. Be prepared to undertake an individual research project. Be prepared to write and submit a scholarly article. Be willing to participate in discussions, presentations and assignments. Review all information carefully before submitting the form. Visit HERE to learn more about the AEE 2026 Fellowship. Conclusion The AEE 2026 Fellowship provides a research- and learning-focused platform centred on the preservation of Ebira knowledge, culture and heritage . The programme brings together individuals with interests spanning history, culture, language, literature, heritage preservation, political studies, development studies and contemporary issues. The fellowship s emphasis on an individual research project and scholarly article makes research and writing important components of the programme. At the same time, its broad range of eligible educational and professional backgrounds allows students, researchers, graduates, early-career professionals, writers and creatives to engage with subjects connected to Ebira knowledge and heritage. Prospective applicants should carefully consider the programme s eight-week weekend commitment and ensure they are prepared to participate in research, discussions, presentations, assignments and other activities. Since the provided application form does not specify a deadline, applicants should verify the latest application information through the official fellowship announcement before submitting their forms. title: Latin American Scholars Grants 2026: Up to £1,750 for Researchers to Attend and Present at the SLAS Conference
summary: The Society for Latin American Studies (SLAS) is offering the Latin American Scholars Grants 2026 , a funding opportunity designed to support scholars based in Latin America who wish to attend the SLAS conference in person, present their research, and develop meaningful academic collaborations with SLAS members. The scheme normally provides 10 awards of up to £1,750 each . The funding is intended to contribute towards eligible costs associated with attending the conference, including registration, travel and accommodation. Although the grant is not expected to cover the full cost of conference participation, recipients can combine the funding with other sources of financial support. The opportunity is particularly relevant to researchers whose work focuses on Latin America and who would benefit from presenting their research internationally, expanding their academic networks and establishing collaborative relationships with scholars connected to SLAS. About the Latin American Scholars Grants The Latin American Scholars Grants are administered by the Society for Latin American Studies (SLAS) as part of its efforts to facilitate greater participation by scholars based in Latin America in its annual conference. The grants are intended to reduce some of the financial barriers associated with international academic conference participation. Successful applicants receive financial assistance towards attending the SLAS conference and are expected to use the opportunity not only to present their research but also to develop closer collaboration with members of the Society. The scheme normally makes ten awards , with each recipient eligible to receive up to £1,750 . Funding can contribute towards: Conference registration costs Travel expenses Accommodation costs Other appropriate costs connected to attending the conference Certain additional care-related expenses where applicable Applicants should understand that the grant is a contribution rather than a full conference sponsorship. SLAS explicitly recognises that £1,750 may not cover the entire cost of attending the conference, meaning applicants may combine the grant with other funding sources where necessary. Who Can Apply for the SLAS Latin American Scholars Grants? The funding scheme is specifically intended for scholars based in Latin America . Applicants must demonstrate that they are based in Latin America through their address and institutional affiliation . The scheme accommodates researchers working in different academic circumstances and does not restrict applications only to scholars holding conventional university positions. Eligible applicants can include: Independent researchers based in Latin America PhD students University-affiliated scholars Researchers affiliated with other academic or research institutions Early-career scholars who meet the relevant requirements Other scholars based in Latin America who are able to participate in the SLAS conference in person Applicants are not required to be members of SLAS in order to apply. However, non-members and other applicants are encouraged to consider joining the Society. Requirement to Attend the Conference in Person One of the central conditions of the funding scheme is that grant recipients must attend the SLAS conference in person . The funding is intended to facilitate physical participation in the conference, including the presentation of the recipient s research and opportunities for networking and collaboration. Award holders must therefore register to attend both days of the conference . This requirement is important for applicants to consider when preparing their budgets and planning their travel. What Does the Grant Fund? Each successful scholar can receive up to £1,750 to contribute towards the costs associated with participating in the conference. The funding may be used to help meet costs such as: Conference Registration A portion of the grant can contribute towards the cost of registering for the SLAS conference. Travel Funding may help scholars meet the costs of travelling to the conference location. Applicants should provide a realistic estimate of anticipated travel expenses in their application. Accommodation The grant can also contribute towards accommodation costs associated with attending the conference. Caring Responsibilities SLAS recognises that caring responsibilities can create additional financial barriers to conference participation. Applicants can therefore include eligible costs associated with caring responsibilities in their proposed budgets. Examples mentioned by SLAS include: Additional care required while the applicant is away Travel expenses for accompanying children Other appropriate costs arising from caring responsibilities Applicants who have such requirements are encouraged to include them in the outline budget rather than excluding them from consideration. SLAS Membership Is Not Mandatory An important feature of the opportunity is that applicants do not have to be SLAS members to apply . Nevertheless, the Society encourages applicants to become members. The grant is particularly focused on building stronger links between scholars based in Latin America and the wider SLAS academic community. Consequently, applicants are expected to explain how the proposed conference participation could create opportunities for collaboration and academic networking. SLAS Member Support Requirement Applications must be supported by a member of SLAS who is not the applicant . This means prospective applicants should identify an SLAS member who can support their application and contribute to the strategic case for the proposed collaboration. The support requirement is connected to one of the main purposes of the scheme: encouraging closer academic relationships between Latin American scholars and members of SLAS. Applicants should therefore approach this part of the application strategically and identify a potential collaborator whose academic interests or expertise have a meaningful connection with their proposed research. What If You Do Not Know an SLAS Member? Applicants who do not already have contacts within SLAS are encouraged to contact Prof Marieke Riethof , former SLAS President, for support. This provides a potential route for researchers who are interested in applying but do not already have an established relationship with an SLAS member. Strategic Case for Collaboration The application should go beyond simply explaining why the applicant needs financial assistance. Applicants are expected to make a strategic case for the proposed collaboration . This is an important component of the selection process because the grant aims to maximise both: Networking opportunities for the applicant. The potential impact of activities associated with the funded trip. A strong application should therefore clearly explain the academic value of attending the conference and the potential benefits of connecting with SLAS members. Applicants may wish to demonstrate: Why their research is relevant to the SLAS community How attending the conference will advance their academic work Which academic connections they hope to develop How the proposed collaboration could develop beyond the conference Why in-person participation is valuable to their research or career development How the funding will enable participation that might otherwise be financially difficult Early-Career Scholar Consideration SLAS aims, wherever possible and where the relevant criteria are met, to reserve two of the awards for early-career scholars . This provision is intended for researchers who are within five years of completing their thesis or dissertation . Applicants who fall within this category should clearly indicate this in their short professional biography. For PhD holders, applicants who are within five years of completing their PhD should therefore make the date of completion clear in their application materials. This information can help the assessment committee determine the applicant s career stage when considering the application. Application Languages The application process provides flexibility regarding language. Completed application forms may be submitted in: English Portuguese Spanish This multilingual application provision is particularly relevant given the geographical focus of the scheme and its aim of supporting scholars based in Latin America. Applicants should nevertheless ensure that all required information is provided clearly and that the application addresses the assessment criteria regardless of the language selected. Assessment Criteria Applications for the Latin American Scholars Grants are assessed using four principal criteria. 1. Strategic Case for Support — 10 Points The strategic case for support carries the highest weighting, with a maximum of 10 points . Applicants should clearly explain the purpose of the proposed conference participation and the potential value of collaboration and networking with SLAS members. The application should demonstrate that the proposed trip has a clear academic and collaborative purpose. 2. Quality of Abstract — 10 Points The quality of the research abstract is also worth 10 points . Applicants should therefore pay close attention to the clarity, relevance and academic quality of the abstract submitted with the application. The abstract should communicate the research topic and its significance effectively while giving the assessment committee a clear understanding of the proposed conference contribution. 3. Profile Relative to Career Stage — 5 Points Applicants can receive up to 5 points for their profile in relation to their career stage. This criterion allows the committee to consider applicants within the context of their academic development. Early-career applicants should ensure that relevant information about their career stage, including whether they completed their PhD within the previous five years, is clearly presented. 4. Justification of Budget — 5 Points The proposed budget is worth 5 points . Applicants should therefore provide a clear and realistic explanation of how the requested funding will be used. A well-prepared budget should distinguish the anticipated expenses and provide sufficient justification for the requested support. Application Timeline Applicants should be aware of the broader timeline surrounding the SLAS conference and the grant application process. October — Conference Call for Papers The deadline for the SLAS conference Call for Papers normally falls in October. SLAS generally aims to notify applicants about whether their conference paper has been accepted before the funding application deadline. However, if the outcome of the Call for Papers has not yet been communicated, applicants are advised to submit the funding application while awaiting the outcome rather than missing the grant deadline. November — Grant Application Deadline The deadline for the Latin American Scholars Grant is in November. For the 2026 application cycle, the stated deadline is: 27 November 2026 Applicants should leave enough time for both the Latin American scholar and the supporting SLAS member to complete the required parts of the application. Applications submitted after the deadline will not be considered. December/January — Notification of Results Applicants will normally be informed of the outcome in December. However, applicants should expect to receive the final notification by the end of January at the latest . February — Conference Registration and Travel Arrangements Successful applicants should then proceed with conference preparations. This stage includes: Registering for the full conference Booking travel Making accommodation arrangements Completing and submitting the grant acceptance form Providing the information required for the SLAS Treasurer to arrange the bank transfer April/May/June — Post-Conference Blog Contribution Grant recipients are expected to prepare and submit a short blog post following their participation. The blog should discuss their conference paper and the research collaboration developed through the funded trip. Post-Grant Blog Requirement Receiving the grant comes with a post-conference communication requirement. Grant recipients are expected to write a blog post of approximately 500–750 words covering: Their conference paper The research collaboration Relevant experiences or outcomes from the funded trip The blog may be published on the SLAS website. The post can be submitted in: English Spanish Portuguese Recipients are encouraged to include photographs or other images where they have the appropriate permissions to use them. The blog should be submitted to the SLAS Secretary within three months of receiving the funding . Encouragement to Publish in the Bulletin of Latin American Research In addition to the blog requirement, SLAS strongly encourages grant recipients to consider submitting an article to the Bulletin of Latin American Research . This provides recipients with an opportunity to develop their conference research into a more substantial academic publication. Applicants and eventual grant recipients should therefore consider how their conference presentation could form part of a broader research and publication strategy. Application Submission and Confirmation Completed application forms should be submitted to the SLAS Secretary before the stated deadline. Applicants will normally receive confirmation that their application has been received within three working days . Applicants should retain evidence of their submission and ensure that they have provided all required information before the deadline. Because applications arriving after the deadline will not be considered under any circumstances, applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their materials. Application Retention and Assessment SLAS states that applications will be retained for up to one year . The applications will be shared with members of the SLAS committee for assessment. Applicants should therefore ensure that their submissions are prepared specifically for the selection criteria and contain information that clearly demonstrates the academic and collaborative value of the proposed conference participation. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants can improve the clarity of their submissions by addressing each assessment criterion directly. 1. Develop a Clear Collaboration Strategy The strategic case is worth the largest number of points, so applicants should clearly explain the proposed collaboration. Rather than focusing exclusively on the need for financial support, explain what academic relationships could result from attending the conference. 2. Prepare a Strong Research Abstract Since the quality of the abstract is worth 10 points, applicants should ensure that the abstract is coherent, focused and representative of the research they intend to present. 3. Explain Your Career Stage Applicants should provide an accurate professional biography and clearly indicate relevant career-stage information. Early-career scholars within five years of completing their thesis or dissertation should make this particularly clear. 4. Prepare a Realistic Budget The budget should be detailed enough for the assessment committee to understand how the £1,750 contribution would be used. Applicants should consider the anticipated costs of: Registration Transportation Accommodation Other legitimate conference-related expenses Eligible caring responsibilities, where applicable 5. Plan the SLAS Member Support Early Because applications require support from an SLAS member, applicants should not leave this requirement until the last minute. Applicants without existing SLAS contacts should consider using the support route suggested by the Society. 6. Consider Other Sources of Funding The grant is not intended to cover the entire cost of attending the conference. Applicants should therefore consider whether university departments, research institutions, professional organisations or other funding bodies can provide additional financial support. APPLY HERE Deadline for the Latin American Scholars Grants The application deadline is: 27 November 2026 Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. Applicants should also allow sufficient time for the supporting SLAS member to complete their part of the application before submission. Why This Opportunity Matters for Latin American Researchers International academic conferences can provide researchers with opportunities to present their work to specialist audiences, receive feedback, develop research collaborations and build professional networks. For scholars based in Latin America, travel and conference costs can present significant barriers to participating in international academic events. The Latin American Scholars Grants seek to address part of this challenge by providing financial assistance while placing particular emphasis on collaboration between scholars based in Latin America and members of SLAS. The combination of financial support, conference participation, networking and potential publication opportunities can make the programme relevant to researchers seeking to expand the international reach of their academic work. Visit HERE to learn more about the Latin American Scholars Grants 2026. Conclusion The SLAS Latin American Scholars Grants 2026 provide up to £1,750 for scholars based in Latin America to contribute towards registration, travel and accommodation costs associated with attending and presenting at the SLAS conference in person. The programme is open to a broad range of scholars, including independent researchers, PhD students and researchers affiliated with universities and other institutions. Applicants do not need to be SLAS members, although membership is encouraged. Each application must be supported by an SLAS member and must present a strategic case for collaboration and networking. The application is assessed on the strategic case for support, quality of the research abstract, the applicant s profile relative to career stage and the justification of the proposed budget. Where criteria are met, two awards are normally reserved for early-career scholars within five years of completing their thesis or dissertation. Applicants should also take note of the post-award requirements, including attending both days of the conference and submitting a 500–750-word blog post about their conference paper and research collaboration within three months of receiving the funding. With the 27 November 2026 deadline approaching, eligible scholars should begin preparing their abstract, collaboration strategy, budget and SLAS member support well in advance of the closing date. title: INTERPOL Paid Internship 2027 in France: €700 Monthly Allowance + Housing & Transport Support
summary: The INTERPOL Paid Internship 2027 in France offers students and recent graduates an opportunity to gain practical international experience within the world s largest international police organization. The Internship – Legal Support to Programmes (LSP) is based at INTERPOL s headquarters in Lyon, France , and provides practical exposure to international legal affairs, data protection, information security, emerging technologies, governance and international police cooperation. The six-month internship is scheduled to begin on 4 January 2027 and is hosted within INTERPOL s Directorate of Legal Support to Operations, Sub-Directorate of Legal Support to Programmes . The position is open to nationals of all 196 INTERPOL member countries . Importantly, this is a paid internship . INTERPOL states that, as of 1 January 2025, interns receive an EUR 700 monthly internship allowance , a EUR 30 monthly transport subsidy , and an additional EUR 170 monthly housing subsidy for eligible interns . INTERPOL Legal Support to Programmes Internship 2027 The Legal Support to Programmes internship is designed for students and recent graduates who want to understand how legal expertise supports the work of an international organization involved in cross-border police cooperation. The position combines legal research and drafting with issues involving technology, data, governance, security and international cooperation. The internship provides an opportunity to work on legal questions associated with INTERPOL s institutional framework and its interactions with member countries and external partners. Key Internship Details Detail Information Organization International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) Internship Legal Support to Programmes (LSP) Directorate Legal Support to Operations Sub-Directorate Legal Support to Programmes Opportunity type Paid Internship Location Lyon, France Duration 6 months Expected start date 4 January 2027 Security clearance Basic Eligible nationalities Nationals of INTERPOL s 196 member countries Working language English Additional INTERPOL languages Arabic, French and Spanish Application deadline 30 September 2026 according to the supplied vacancy Monthly internship allowance EUR 700 Transport subsidy EUR 30 per month Housing subsidy EUR 170 per month for eligible interns INTERPOL s general internship information confirms that its internships normally last between six and 11 months, with most opportunities based at its headquarters in Lyon, France. About INTERPOL The International Criminal Police Organization , commonly known as INTERPOL, facilitates international police cooperation between its member countries. The organization works with law enforcement authorities and other relevant organizations to support efforts to prevent and combat international crime. Its work covers a wide range of transnational crime and security issues, including terrorism, organized crime, cybercrime and financial crime. Because INTERPOL operates across national borders and deals with sensitive information and cooperation between different jurisdictions, its activities require a substantial legal and regulatory framework. The Legal Support to Programmes team contributes to this environment by providing legal support relating to areas such as data protection, information security, governance, emerging technologies and cooperation with external entities. This makes the internship particularly relevant to candidates interested in the intersection of law, technology, international organizations, data governance and international cooperation . What the INTERPOL Internship Offers The INTERPOL Internship Programme is designed to give students and recent graduates practical experience within an international organization. INTERPOL explains that its internship programme provides interns with an opportunity to understand the organization s objectives, learn how international police cooperation is organized, gain practical work experience and develop skills relevant to future employment. It also provides experience in a multicultural, multidisciplinary and multi-ethnic working environment. For the Legal Support to Programmes position, these benefits are connected specifically to legal and governance work. 1. Paid International Work Experience The internship is financially supported through an internship allowance. As of 1 January 2025, INTERPOL states that interns receive: EUR 700 per month internship allowance EUR 30 per month transport subsidy EUR 170 per month housing subsidy for eligible interns The EUR 700 allowance is prorated according to the number of days worked. Therefore, an eligible intern receiving all three forms of support could receive up to EUR 900 per month in combined allowance and subsidies. However, this should not be described as a fully funded internship . INTERPOL states that costs related to recruitment, travel, insurance, accommodation and living expenses must be borne by the intern. Interns are also responsible for obtaining and financing the required visa. 2. Practical Legal Experience The internship allows participants to move beyond academic study and gain practical experience working on legal questions within an international institution. The intern will conduct research, assist with drafting documents and support the Legal Support to Programmes team on a variety of legal and institutional matters. This can help candidates develop practical skills in legal research, analysis, drafting and institutional documentation. 3. Exposure to International Legal Frameworks The internship provides exposure to the legal framework governing INTERPOL and its relationship with member countries. This can be particularly useful for students and recent graduates interested in: Public international law International organizations International cooperation International criminal justice Global governance Cross-border legal frameworks 4. Exposure to Data Protection and Information Security Data protection and information security are central components of the internship s learning objectives. Because INTERPOL s work involves international cooperation and information processing, the legal framework surrounding the use, protection and processing of information is an important area of work. Interns can therefore gain exposure to legal issues involving: Data protection Information security Processing of data Institutional compliance Information governance 5. Emerging Technology Regulation The internship also provides exposure to the legal and regulatory issues surrounding emerging technologies . This is particularly relevant for candidates interested in the rapidly developing relationship between technology and law. Candidates with prior exposure to technology regulation, information security or data protection can demonstrate how these areas relate to the internship. 6. International and Multicultural Experience INTERPOL operates in an international environment involving professionals from different countries and disciplines. The internship therefore provides experience working in a multicultural, multidisciplinary and multi-ethnic environment . This can help interns develop professional communication, collaboration, adaptability and cross-cultural working skills. Learning Objectives of the Internship The Legal Support to Programmes internship has three principal learning objectives. Understanding data protection and information security The intern will gain knowledge and practical exposure to legal frameworks related to data protection and information security. Understanding INTERPOL s legal framework The intern will develop an understanding of the legal framework governing INTERPOL and its interactions with its member countries. Understanding legal issues related to international crime The intern will gain exposure to legal aspects associated with different crime areas, including: Terrorism Organized crime Cybercrime Financial crime Other areas of international criminal cooperation The combination of these areas gives the internship a broad legal and institutional focus. Primary Duties and Responsibilities The selected intern will support the Legal Support to Programmes team with a range of legal and governance-related tasks. 1. Conduct Legal Research A major responsibility will be conducting legal research and assisting with drafting responses to various legal questions. The work may involve questions concerning: INTERPOL s Constitution INTERPOL s Rules on the Processing of Data Operational support provided to member countries Data protection Information security Partnerships with external entities Cooperation arrangements This responsibility can help the intern develop practical research and legal-analysis skills in an international institutional context. 2. Assist With Governance Documents The intern will also assist with research and drafting for governance-related documents. Examples listed in the vacancy include: Risk assessment guides Frequently Asked Questions Standard Operating Procedures Other governance documentation This part of the internship may be particularly relevant to candidates interested in compliance, governance, risk management and technology policy. 3. Support Cooperation Agreements The intern will provide support to staff working on the drafting and negotiation of cooperation agreements and other cooperative arrangements between INTERPOL and its partners. This can expose the intern to the practical process of developing institutional agreements and managing relationships between international organizations and external entities. 4. Perform Other Assigned Duties The intern may also be required to undertake other tasks assigned by the supervisor according to the needs of the Legal Support to Programmes team. This means the precise day-to-day work may vary depending on ongoing projects and priorities. Who Can Apply? The internship is open to nationals of all 196 INTERPOL member countries . INTERPOL s general internship criteria require applicants to: Be enrolled in a post-secondary accredited academic institution, or have graduated from one within the previous year at the time of application. Be a national of an INTERPOL member country. Have reached the legal age of majority in their country of nationality. Be fluent in English. Meet the additional requirements specified for the particular internship. For this specific Legal Support to Programmes position, the vacancy indicates a preference for candidates who have completed coursework related to technology, data protection or public international law . Academic Requirements Applicants must either currently be studying at a recognized post-secondary institution or have graduated from such an institution within the previous year. Relevant academic backgrounds may include areas connected to: Law Public international law Technology law Data protection Information security Emerging technology regulation International relations where relevant legal coursework has been completed Other related fields where the candidate can demonstrate a connection to the internship The vacancy specifically identifies coursework related to technology, data protection or public international law as preferable. Nationality and Geographic Eligibility The internship is not restricted to applicants from a particular continent or region. The vacancy states that INTERPOL s Internship Programme welcomes candidates from all 196 member countries . Consequently, eligible applicants can come from countries across: Africa Asia Europe North America South America Central America and the Caribbean Oceania The relevant requirement is nationality in an INTERPOL member country , rather than belonging to a particular race, ethnicity or continent. INTERPOL also actively encourages applications from women and nationals of member countries that are currently underrepresented among its staff. Language Requirements English Professional fluency in English is required for the position. Applicants should therefore be comfortable with professional written and spoken English, particularly because the work involves legal research, drafting and communication. Other INTERPOL Languages Knowledge of another INTERPOL official language is considered an asset. These include: French Spanish Arabic Knowledge of one or more of these languages may therefore strengthen a candidate s profile, although professional fluency in English is the stated requirement. Technical Skills Applicants should have a working knowledge of Microsoft Office tools . This is relevant because the internship involves research, drafting, documentation and other professional tasks that require standard office applications. Candidates should also consider highlighting relevant digital and research skills in their application where appropriate. Professional Competencies Beyond academic qualifications, applicants are expected to demonstrate professional qualities suited to legal work within an international organization. The vacancy identifies the following abilities: Discretion Diplomacy Tact Rigor Willingness to learn Ability to work with unfamiliar areas of law These qualities are particularly relevant because the internship may involve sensitive information, complex legal questions and interactions with different institutional stakeholders. Additional Assets Prior exposure to the following areas is considered an advantage: Data protection law Information security Regulation of emerging technologies Governance documentation Technical documentation Risk management documentation Emerging technology-related regulatory work Applicants do not need to demonstrate advanced professional experience in every one of these areas. However, relevant academic coursework, research, projects or previous experience can be useful when demonstrating suitability. Internship Allowance and Financial Support One of the most important features of this opportunity is that it is a paid internship . INTERPOL s current general internship conditions state that, as of 1 January 2025 , the internship allowance is EUR 700 , prorated according to the number of days worked. Interns also receive a EUR 30 monthly transport subsidy , while eligible interns can receive an additional EUR 170 monthly housing subsidy . This means: Base internship allowance: EUR 700/month Transport subsidy: EUR 30/month Housing subsidy for eligible interns: EUR 170/month Potential combined monthly support: Up to EUR 900/month The housing subsidy is subject to eligibility, so applicants should not automatically assume that the full EUR 170 will apply to them. Learn More HERE Health Insurance INTERPOL requires interns to have health insurance coverage for the entire duration of the internship. The organization s general internship conditions state that interns are eligible to request enrolment in INTERPOL s health insurance coverage at no additional cost. Applicants should nevertheless carefully review the applicable insurance requirements and conditions before beginning the internship. Location: Lyon, France The internship is based in Lyon, France , where INTERPOL has its headquarters. Working in Lyon provides the intern with an opportunity to experience an international institutional environment while working alongside professionals involved in legal, operational and support functions. Because this is an in-person duty station, applicants should consider the practical implications of relocating to France, including accommodation, travel, visa requirements and living expenses. INTERPOL s general internship information confirms that most of its internships are based at its headquarters in Lyon, although some internships may be offered at other duty stations. Internship Duration and Start Date The Legal Support to Programmes internship has a stated duration of six months . The estimated starting date is: 4 January 2027 The internship is therefore suitable for candidates who can make themselves available for a six-month placement beginning in January 2027. Security Clearance and Confidentiality Requirements Because INTERPOL works with sensitive information, selected candidates are subject to a confidentiality vetting process before their appointment is confirmed. If selected, candidates must provide a certificate of non-criminal records from: Their country of nationality; and Any other country in which they have lived for more than 12 months during the previous five years. The certificate must cover the relevant criminal-record requirements specified by the organization. Candidates who progress to the interview stage are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the process of obtaining these documents in the countries concerned. Doing this early can help prevent delays if an offer is eventually made. Interns are also required to maintain confidentiality regarding unpublished information obtained during their internship. INTERPOL s general internship conditions emphasize discretion and confidentiality. Application Process Applications must be submitted through INTERPOL s recruitment platform in response to the specific internship vacancy. INTERPOL states that applications must be made through its Recruitment Hub and that candidates should include a cover letter addressing their motivation, suitability and expectations. APPLY HERE What the Cover Letter Should Address The application should include a cover letter explaining: 1. Motivation to Join INTERPOL Explain why you are interested in undertaking an internship with INTERPOL and what attracts you to the organization s international mission. 2. Interest in the Legal Support to Programmes Internship Explain why this specific internship is relevant to your academic background and professional interests. For example, candidates could connect their interests to: International law Data protection Information security Technology regulation International organizations Governance International cooperation 3. Relevant Strengths and Assets Applicants should clearly demonstrate the skills and knowledge they would bring to the position. These may include: Legal research Legal writing Policy analysis Academic research Data protection knowledge Technology-related knowledge Microsoft Office skills Multilingual abilities Previous exposure to governance or risk documentation 4. Expectations for the Internship Explain what you hope to learn and how the internship fits into your academic and professional development. A strong application should connect the applicant s existing background with the specific learning objectives of the internship. Assessment and Selection Process INTERPOL states that applications are assessed against the requirements identified in the vacancy. Candidates whose qualifications and profiles most closely meet the requirements may be contacted directly by the hiring manager for further consideration and assessment. The selection process is therefore based on the qualifications of applicants and the needs of the organization. INTERPOL also states that it does not discriminate on any grounds and that candidates are treated under conditions of equality. INTERPOL and University Internship Agreements An important point for applicants is that INTERPOL does not establish or endorse internship agreements with universities or academic institutions for these internships. Internship arrangements and communication are made directly between INTERPOL and the individual selected for the internship. Applicants should therefore be cautious of anyone claiming to represent INTERPOL and requesting money to arrange or secure the internship. Application Fees and Fraud Prevention Applicants should never pay an individual or organization to submit an application or secure this internship. INTERPOL s official internship information directs applicants to its recruitment platform for applications. Candidates should rely on INTERPOL s official recruitment channels and verify any communication claiming to come from the organization. How to Prepare a Strong Application Candidates can improve the clarity of their applications by carefully matching their experience to the requirements of the Legal Support to Programmes position. 1. Demonstrate relevant academic preparation Identify coursework, research projects, dissertations or academic assignments connected to law, international law, data protection, technology or information security. 2. Highlight legal research and writing The role involves significant legal research and drafting. Applicants should therefore demonstrate their ability to: Find and analyze legal information Conduct structured research Interpret complex material Draft clear documents Present findings professionally 3. Connect technology and law The vacancy specifically identifies data protection, information security and emerging technology regulation as useful areas of prior exposure. Candidates with relevant coursework or projects should make these connections clear. 4. Demonstrate discretion and professionalism The role involves sensitive institutional information, so applicants should show evidence of professional judgment, confidentiality, accuracy and attention to detail. 5. Tailor the cover letter Avoid submitting a generic cover letter. The application should specifically address the Legal Support to Programmes position and explain why the applicant s background matches the internship s learning objectives and responsibilities. 6. Review the financial implications Because the internship is paid but not fully funded, applicants should carefully consider travel, accommodation, visa and living costs in Lyon before accepting an offer. INTERPOL explicitly states that these costs are the responsibility of the intern. Because closing dates can change and employers may close vacancies earlier, applicants should verify the current deadline directly through INTERPOL s official Recruitment Hub before submitting an application. INTERPOL s official internship page directs applicants to its Recruitment Hub for current internship vacancies. Conclusion The INTERPOL Legal Support to Programmes Internship 2027 is a paid international internship designed for students and recent graduates who want practical experience in legal affairs within an international organization. Based in Lyon, France , the six-month placement provides exposure to legal research, legal drafting, data protection, information security, emerging technology regulation, governance documentation and cooperation agreements. It also offers insight into the legal framework supporting international police cooperation. The financial package includes a EUR 700 monthly internship allowance , a EUR 30 monthly transport subsidy , and an additional EUR 170 monthly housing subsidy for eligible interns . However, applicants should understand that the opportunity is paid rather than fully funded , as INTERPOL states that interns are responsible for travel, accommodation, living, insurance and visa-related costs. Eligibility extends to nationals of all 196 INTERPOL member countries , provided they meet the academic, age, language and position-specific requirements. The specific vacancy is particularly relevant to candidates with coursework or experience related to technology, data protection or public international law . Candidates interested in the position should prepare a tailored application and cover letter demonstrating their motivation, relevant qualifications, interest in the Legal Support to Programmes function and expectations for the internship. They should also prepare for the organization s confidentiality and security-clearance requirements. The vacancy states an application deadline of 30 September 2026 , although the third-party listing supplied for this article displays 1 October 2026 .
